nodes.question: How have hydromorphological restoration projects performed in terms of success?
nodes.answer: They have shown varying degrees of success, with some studies reporting positive outcomes and others finding minimal or no improvements beyond the local habitat scale.
nodes.paragraph: Ecological Processes (2025) 14:30 It is widely believed that the recovery of benthic inver - tebrate assemblages in Europe has primarily resulted from improvements in water quality (Haase et al. 2023; Sinclair et al. 2024). While water quality enhancements have undoubtedly played a crucial role, the relationship between these improvements and broader ecological out - comes is more complex than it might appear, especially at larger scales. This complexity raises critical questions about additional factors that influence ecological recov - ery. For instance, hydromorphological restoration pro - jects, which aim to restore physical habitat conditions, have shown varying degrees of success (Kail et al. 2015; Lu et al. 2019). While some studies report positive out - comes (e.g., Feld et al. 2018; Li et al. 2018), others find minimal or no improvements beyond the local habitat scale (e.g., Verdonschot et al. 2016; White et al. 2017). This inconsistency highlights a significant challenge: despite substantial advances in wastewater treatment and water quality, hydromorphological restoration often falls short of achieving ecological recovery.
